ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: (2018 Zhejiang Four-City Joint Exam) As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of a Van de Graaff generator. The positive charge of the DC high-voltage power supply, through brush E, the conveyor belt, and brush F, is continuously transferred to the outer surface of the spherical shell, and may be regarded as being uniformly distributed on the outer surface, thereby forming a high voltage between the metal spherical shell and the earth. Regarding points A and B on the metal spherical shell, which of the following judgments is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The electric potentials at points A and B are the same

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of a Van de Graaff generator. The positive charge of the DC high-voltage power supply is continuously transferred to the outer surface of the spherical shell through brush E, the conveyor belt, and brush F, and may be regarded as being uniformly distributed on the outer surface, thereby forming a high voltage between the metal spherical shell and the earth. ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The electric potentials at points A and B are the same
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of a Van de Graaff generator. At the top there is a spherical metal shell labeled “metal spherical shell,” and positive charges are drawn distributed near the outer surface of the spherical shell; point A is marked near the top outer surface of the spherical shell, and point B is marked near the right-side outer surface of the spherical shell; the two belong to the same metal spherical shell. In the figure, the conveyor belt, brush E, brush F, insulating support, and the label connected to the positive electrode of the high-voltage power supply can also be seen. Reasoning: The problem statement explains that the positive charge of the DC high-voltage power supply is continuously transferred to the outer surface of the spherical shell via brush E, the conveyor belt, and brush F, and may be regarded as uniformly distributed, causing a high voltage to form between the metal spherical shell and the earth. The metal spherical shell, as a conductor, is an equipotential body as a whole when in electrostatic equilibrium, that is, the potentials at all points on the surface and inside of the same metal conductor are the same. Therefore, the electric potentials at points A and B located on the same metal spherical shell are the same.
